detail.title: Thematic Evolution and Collaboration Networks in Character Education: A Bibliometric Perspective
detail.abstract: This study seeks to map the dynamics of publication, thematic evolution, and international collaboration in character education research, while also identifying dominant knowledge structures and future research directions aligned with digital ethics and Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education). As education systems confront complex challenges including cyberbullying, disinformation, academic dishonesty, and AI-mediated ethical dilemmas character education has gained strategic relevance. However, its intellectual landscape and global interconnectivity remain underexplored. Using a bibliometric approach based on the Scopus database (2020–2026; article type; English language), an initial pool of 15,295 records was screened according to eligibility criteria, yielding a final dataset of 723 articles. Data were analysed using Biblioshiny (Bibliometrix-R) to examine publication trends, disciplinary distribution, influential sources and authors, keyword co-occurrence, thematic development, and international co-authorship networks. Findings indicate a steady increase in scholarly interest, with publications rising from approximately 135 documents in 2020 to over 150 in 2024, before declining slightly in 2025–2026. The field is dominated by Social Sciences (29.9%), followed by Computer Science (13.6%) and Arts & Humanities (9.7%), reflecting its multidisciplinary growth. Indonesia (~200 documents), China (~170), and the United States (>110) are the most prolific contributors. Thematic analysis highlights emerging clusters in digital ethics, socio-emotional literacy, and the integration of local cultural values. Strong linkages between “collaboration networks”, “bibliometric analysis”, and “character education” were also identified as motor themes. In sum, this longitudinal bibliometric analysis offers empirical insights to inform curriculum innovation, policy development, and future research. Strengthening international collaboration and embedding ethical, technology-informed pedagogies are critical to addressing contemporary moral challenges and advancing SDG 4.

detail.abstract: We extend social identity theory to study human-AI trade-offs in hiring contexts. In a baseline experiment, representative U.S. participants allocate tasks between a human worker and either another human, ChatGPT, or the foreign model DeepSeek, with explicitly varied productivity. On average, people incur costs to under-allocate tasks to AI, particularly DeepSeek. Two additional experiments, inducing identities on workers via minimal-group and political affiliations, reveal a hierarchy: in-group humans receive the most, followed comparably by out-group humans and in-group AI, and out-group AI receives the fewest. Individual perceived social distance to AI and groupy tendency jointly shape the task allocation decisions.

title: Path to Viksit Bharat: A Seven-Phase Analysis of India's Economic Transformation, 1947-2025
affiliations: Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics

detail.title: Path to Viksit Bharat: A Seven-Phase Analysis of India's Economic Transformation, 1947-2025
detail.abstract: The paper analyses India's economic development from 1947 to 2025 through a seven-phase framework capturing major shifts in policy orientation, institutional evolution, and structural transformation. The study has used a qualitative historical-analytical design supported by secondary data from national statistical sources and international databases, the study traces India's transition from a state-led, agrarian economy to a service-led emerging market. The analysis shows that while the Green Revolution, the 1991 liberalisation reforms, and the post-2000 IT expansion generated significant productivity gains and enabled global integration, India's structural transformation has remained incomplete. Manufacturing has stagnated, labour absorption has been limited, and regional and gender disparities have persisted despite recent improvements in digital governance, financial inclusion, and public service delivery. The paper contributes to the development studies literature by integrating long-term historical evidence with contemporary policy outcomes to highlight the interaction between institutional reforms, sectoral dynamics, and distributional challenges. The findings suggest that realising the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 requires a strategic shift toward employment-intensive industrialisation, human capital strengthening, expansion of female labour force participation, agricultural modernisation, and greater investment in innovation and climate resilience. The study provides a synthesised framework for understanding India's development trajectory and outlines policy priorities for achieving inclusive and sustainable high-income growth.

title: Risk Factor Disclosure Summaries
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Risk Factor Disclosure Summaries
detail.abstract: Since 2005, the SEC has mandated that firms include Risk Factor Disclosures (RFDs) in annual 10-K filings. In 2020, this mandate was “modernized” and now requires the inclusion of a two-page summary section for RFDs longer than 15 pages. On the one hand, the SEC contends that this summary requirement should benefit investors, especially those who have less time to review and analyze registrants’ disclosure. On the other hand, firms may not include all material risks in a summary, and, if some investors fixate on summaries, gaps in understanding risks may widen among investors. We use summaries generated by a large language model (LLM) as a benchmark to examine the information content of firm-disclosed summaries. Our evidence suggests that, relative to the LLM-generated summaries, firm-disclosed summaries are more positively toned, less specific, easier to read, and more likely to omit firm-idiosyncratic risks such as strategic, legal, and human-capital risks. Our results also suggest that summaries that deviate more from the LLM benchmark are associated with higher information asymmetry, uncertainty, and disagreement around the 10-K filing date. These effects do not appear to be explained by changes in risks disclosed in the full RFD surrounding the Modernization or lookahead bias in our benchmark summary generation. Overall, our results suggest that the summary requirement in the SEC’s 2020 Modernization may have led to unintended negative consequences, at least over the initial years that are covered by our sample.

title: Locally Conservative, Globally Not: Diagnosing the Lagrangian Structure of Pretrained Transformers

detail.title: Locally Conservative, Globally Not: Diagnosing the Lagrangian Structure of Pretrained Transformers

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. This research was conducted independently, outside the scope of any employment, with no external funding, no financial relationships with any organization relevant to the subject of this work, and no personal relationships that could be perceived to have influenced the study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This research involves no human participants, patient data, clinical studies, or personal data of any kind. All experiments were conducted on publicly available pretrained language models (GPT-2, Pythia) and synthetic text corpora.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding. This research was self-funded and conducted independently.

detail.abstract: We give an exact mechanical interpretation of the cosine Semantic Tube Prediction (STP) loss of Huang et al. (2026) and use it to construct a static architectural diagnostic for the global Lagrangian structure of pretrained transformers. The mathematical core is the closed-form identity  L_STP = 1 − √(1 − |a⊥|² / |d₂|²) , which relates the cosine STP loss between three consecutive hidden states to the magnitude of the component of acceleration normal to the trajectory; we prove the identity algebraically and verify it to machine precision across 1,314 consecutive triplets on GPT-2. Two structural consequences follow immediately: STP loss is blind to the tangential component of acceleration, which we measure to be approximately twice the normal component on GPT-2, and deceleration along the trajectory is the direct mechanical signature of a learned restoring force, with 97.9% of triplets decelerating and a permutation null at z <-11 establishing that sequential token order produces significantly smoother trajectories than random orderings. Both findings replicate on Pythia-160M. These descriptive results establish local hallmarks of damped Lagrangian flow on a bounded attractive potential as a property of trained attention transformers. The natural follow-up-whether the per-layer hidden-state updates globally derive from a single shared scalar potential-is empirically testable. We fit the joint regression Δh_ℓ ≈ α_ℓ · v_ℓ − β_ℓ · ∇V_ψ(h_ℓ) across all layers with a single learned V ψ on frozen checkpoints, and obtain a three-way architectural separator on Tiny Shakespeare: a weight-tied scalar-potential autoregressive flow (used here as a positive control) attains median per-layer test R 2 = 0.957 with a uniform layer profile; a scale-and data-matched 8M-parameter GPT-2-style decoder reaches R 2 = 0.54 with monotonic decay; pretrained GPT-2 small reaches R 2 = 0.46 with a bathtub profile (middle-band mean 0.09). Three independent controls rule out alternative explanations: an oracle fit using the positive control's own potential attains R 2 = 0.931 on the LayerNorm variant (and 1.0000 on the base architecture); a V ψ capacity sweep over a 16× parameter band rules out expressivity limitation; and the separation reproduces under orthogonal token-direction coordinates. All three architectures pass a velocity-aware Jacobian-symmetry test at PCA-16, making local per-step conservativity universal while global shared-potential structure remains architectural. We therefore characterise the Lagrangian content of trained attention transformers as locally conservative but globally not derivable from a shared scalar potential. We provide both a sharper reading of what STP-style training objectives do and do not measure, and a reproducible architectural diagnostic that other globally-Lagrangian designs can be evaluated against.

title: Born Too Early: Perceived Recency Discontinuity and Scientific Recognition
affiliations: and Dalian University of Technology

detail.title: Born Too Early: Perceived Recency Discontinuity and Scientific Recognition

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no competing interests.

detail.abstract: Temporal labels, such as years, months, and quarters, are common ways of representing time, yet they are often treated as neutral background information. We find evidence of a temporal-labeling mechanism in which coarse-grained labels divide continuous time into discrete stages, making adjacent objects appear more or less recent than they objectively are and thereby shaping judgment and choice. We define this label-induced discontinuity in recognition as the Perceived Recency Discontinuity (PRD) effect. We formalize how temporal labels transform objective age into subjective age and generate perceived recency differences that can affect behavior. Scientific citation provides an especially suitable setting for observing the PRD effect. Using 71,257 FT50 journal papers and more than 13.61 million citation events, we construct a regression discontinuity design around year boundaries. Papers published just before a year boundary receive about 14 fewer citations within five years than those published just after it, corresponding to a 19.6% citation advantage for papers on the right side of the boundary. A behavioral experiment on reference selection provides micro-level evidence consistent with the interpretation that year labels shift perceived recency. The findings show that formal temporal labels are institutionalized signals that shape judgment, opportunity allocation, and downstream outcomes.

title: Key Patents and Economic Performance: Patent Quality, Technological Innovation, and Growth in Knowledge-Based Economies
affiliations: and

detail.title: Key Patents and Economic Performance: Patent Quality, Technological Innovation, and Growth in Knowledge-Based Economies
detail.abstract:
In knowledge-based economies, technological innovation capability, intangible assets, and intellectual property are becoming increasingly important for long-term economic performance. Patent data are widely used as indicators of innovation; however, simple patent counts do not adequately capture the quality, technological relevance, or international market coverage of individual patents. This paper therefore examines the extent to which key patents can serve as a quality-oriented indicator of technological innovation capability for analysing economic performance. Key patents are understood as particularly high-quality patents in relevant key technologies, whose patent strength derives from technological relevance and international market coverage.

The paper combines a conceptual analysis of the key patent approach with literature from growth and innovation economics, as well as with an exploratory empirical plausibility assessment based on a global patent dataset on world-class patents in future technologies (Breitinger et al., 2020). Economic performance is operationalised empirically through per capita income. The empirical evidence is assessed from two complementary perspectives: an international cross-section of high-income economies and a dynamic analysis of the United States, which held a particularly prominent position in high-quality patenting across key future technologies during the period under observation. In both perspectives, the findings point to a positive association between key patents and per capita income. They should not, however, be interpreted as evidence of causality, but as empirically grounded support for the plausibility of this relationship.

The contribution of this paper lies in positioning key patents as a differentiated innovation indicator that takes patent quality, technological relevance, and international reach more fully into account than mere patent volumes. The key patent approach thus offers a scientifically grounded perspective on innovation capability and economic performance in knowledge-based economies.

detail.abstract: In this contribution, I discuss the perceptions, experiences and impact of time in the lives and journeys of people who have left Iran to escape persecution or discrimination on SOGIESC grounds. By analysing semi-structured interviews and poetry workshops carried out with migrants and other stakeholders in the project ‘Negotiating Queer Identities Following Forced Migration’ (https://iranqueerefugee.net/), I explore the role of time in the journeys of queer Iranians in exile in three country case studies generally seen as being of transition (Turkey), destination (UK) or resettlement (Canada). Against the background of literature on the role of time in migration law and policy, I examine how time is a constant concern in the experiences of queer Iranians in exile, but how it simultaneously manifests in positive ways. This piece thereby makes an empirically and theoretically-based original contribution to the literature on time and migration by highlighting the productively contradictory experiences of time.

title:

detail.title:
When Systems Reject their Leaders: A Cybernetic Analysis of Project Cybersyn and the Limits of Public Sector Leadership
Development
detail.abstract:
This paper addresses a persistent contradiction in public leadership development: substantial investment in competency-based leadership programs has not consistently translated into system-level transformation. Recent scholarship increasingly argues that leadership development remains theoretically fragmented and conceptually underdeveloped (Marcy, 2023). Existing approaches largely assume that stronger leaders produce stronger institutions. Yet highly capable leaders and sophisticated interventions frequently fail to generate sustainable change in complex public systems.

Using Project Cybersyn as a theory-driven case, this study examines why leadership-driven innovation may fail despite exceptional expertise and advanced system design. The paper proposes meta-capacity as a system-level construct and integrates it with the Systemic Hierarchy of Value and Scale (SHVS) framework. It argues that leadership effectiveness depends not only on leadership capability itself, but on the alignment between intervention complexity and the capacity of hierarchical systems to absorb, coordinate, and sustain change.

The study reframes leadership failure as a problem of systemic misalignment rather than individual deficit, offering a new explanation for why highly capable leaders and advanced reforms may fail to produce sustainable transformation in complex public systems.

title: The Gender Gap on the Socio-cultural Cleavage
affiliations: , University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Political Science Department, Centre for Socio-Political Data and University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

detail.title: The Gender Gap on the Socio-cultural Cleavage

declarations.ethicsApproval: Obtained ethical approval for the subject study (survey and interviews) conducted in The Netherlands.

detail.abstract: This paper explains the contemporary gender gap in voting as a life-course outcome of gendered sorting in education and work. Drawing on social role theory, we argue that the gender gap is linked to the division of labor in which women and men disproportionately enter different fields of study and occupational environments. We test the effect of socialization in education and work using cross-national surveys and longitudinal panels. Sequential mediation analysis shows that differences in educational and occupational field account for a substantial share of the gender gap in voting on the socio-cultural cleavage. Within-person panel estimates indicate that entering higher education, especially into fields with high cultural-communicative content, is followed by shifts toward socio-liberal or GAL/Green support. Gendered pathways through education and employment help to translate contrasting roles in the division of labor into the contemporary gender gap.

detail.abstract: The term 'housing system' is increasingly used in housing debates but remains comparatively underdefined, underexplored and under-visualised. Moreover, policy and practice tend to favour a siloed tenure-based approach, contributing to system-level incoherence and unequal and unintended housing outcomes. This is problematic in the context of the Scottish housing emergency. A key challenge in addressing these limitations is that the housing system is complex and difficult to conceptualise and comprehend. Adopting a systems perspective, this paper responds to the challenge through the development of a heuristic model of the Scottish housing system, which can help policymakers and practitioners to visualise and better understand the system as a whole, ultimately allowing for more coherent interventions and practice. The model brings together sources of demand and supply, system levers and support mechanisms, system barriers, and detrimental housing outcomes within a single visual framework. The model is intended as an exploratory heuristic framework designed to support housing system visualisation and policy discussion, while presenting opportunities for future development and comparative application.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Dialogic Eating (Taiwagata Inshoku)—a practice‑based methodology developed at FabCafe Osaka that uses food and drink experience as a protocol for opening, sharing, and translating pre‑verbal sensory knowledge. Departing from the established framework of Visual Thinking Strategies (VTS) and dialogic art appreciation, Dialogic Eating addresses a structural access problem: while art‑based dialogue methods are cognitively effective, they presuppose aesthetic literacy that creates participation barriers, particularly in Japan, where a national survey found that 35.4% of cultural nonparticipants cited “no interest” as the primary reason, with a further 22.8% giving no specific reason—together representing 58.2% with no orientation toward cultural engagement (Agency for Cultural Affairs, 2019). Eating and drinking, by contrast, are universal embodied experiences requiring no prior cultural knowledge.

Drawing on four practice programs implemented with approximately 256 participants—the Anparfait tasting experience, the Hon wo Nomu (Drinking Books) series, the Kemono Ato Michi (Beast Trail) program, and professional Dialogic Eating salon sessions—as well as neuroscientific research on olfactory‑triggered autobiographical memory, this paper proposes a three‑function model of Dialogic Eating: (1) sensory translation, (2) relational generation, and (3) connection to urban experience design.

Two practitioner‑derived findings extend existing theory: a four‑stage engagement sequence that emerges consistently when participants encounter an unnamed stimulus, activating an investigative rather than confirmatory mode of perception; and a sensibility‑switching effect in which the shift in perceptual register induced by Dialogic Eating persists beyond the session, with implications for perceptual education and organizational culture change. The paper situates these findings within the framework of Sensibility Urbanism (Kansei Toshi‑ron), arguing that Dialogic Eating constitutes a methodology for accessing and articulating the embodied knowledge of urban value that conventional metrics cannot capture.

title: Recursive Coordination Capitalism: Programmable Demand Architectures and Innovation Governance in AI-Scale Economies

detail.title: Recursive Coordination Capitalism: Programmable Demand Architectures and Innovation Governance in AI-Scale Economies
detail.abstract: This paper develops a theoretical framework for understanding purpose-bound money (PBM) as a programmable coordination architecture for AI-scale economies. Unlike conventional monetary systems, which primarily function as generalized exchange and stabilization mechanisms, PBM systems can structure future demand, influence technological diffusion, reduce investment uncertainty, and coordinate long-term innovation dynamics. Building on endogenous growth theory, Schumpeterian creative destruction, capability theory, and computational governance, the paper introduces the concept of Recursive Coordination Capitalism: an emerging economic regime in which technological progress, human capability formation, corporate investment, and institutional adaptation become recursively aligned through programmable demand architectures. The analysis argues that AI-scale economies intensify coordination problems involving innovation timing, labor transition, adoption velocity, and market concentration. In this context, programmable monetary systems may function as adaptive coordination infrastructures capable of accelerating frontier-technology diffusion, stabilizing long-horizon investment, and partially governing technological transition dynamics. At the same time, the paper emphasizes the institutional risks of programmable economic systems, including surveillance expansion, algorithmic governance failure, and excessive centralization. It therefore proposes constitutional computational governance principles centered on democratic oversight, privacy-preserving computation, transparency, decentralization, reversibility, and institutional contestability. The paper concludes that purpose-bound money is not merely a welfare tool, digital currency, or industrial policy instrument, but a programmable coordination infrastructure capable of recursively aligning technological innovation, corporate growth, and human flourishing in increasingly complex AI-scale economies.

title: International Trade Law and Gender Linkages: A Gender Perspective on Non‑Tariff Measures in Malawi

detail.title: International Trade Law and Gender Linkages: A Gender Perspective on Non‑Tariff Measures in Malawi
detail.abstract: The relationship between international trade and gender equality has become increasingly significant in international economic law and development policy. While trade liberalisation has traditionally been viewed as gender-neutral, contemporary scholarship demonstrates that trade policies and regulatory mechanisms affect women and men differently due to existing socioeconomic inequalities. This article examines the gendered impact of non-tariff measures (NTMs) in Malawi, focusing particularly on sanitary and phytosanitary measures, customs procedures, rules of origin, product standards, and digital trade facilitation. Using Malawi as a case study, the article argues that NTMs disproportionately burden women traders, especially those engaged in informal cross-border trade and small-scale agriculture. At the same time, the article demonstrates that gender-responsive trade interventions, digital trade facilitation tools, and voluntary sustainability standards can significantly improve women's economic participation. The article further analyses the evolving international legal framework on trade and gender within the World Trade Organization (WTO), the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), and regional trade arrangements in Southern Africa. It concludes by proposing policy recommendations for integrating gender perspectives into Malawi's trade governance framework.

title: The Anthropological Trap of Digital Utopia: From Cybernetic Socialism to the Crisis of Platform Democracy

detail.title: The Anthropological Trap of Digital Utopia: From Cybernetic Socialism to the Crisis of Platform Democracy
detail.abstract: Digital utopias fail in structurally predictable ways. This paper argues that what makes them predictable is anthropological mis-specification: the systematic encoding of a false model of the human subject-rational, autonomous, informed, capable of sustained deliberation under growing complexity-into the architecture of governance systems. This assumption is not an accidental error or ideological distortion. It is a structural feature that persisted across five decades of digital utopianism, from Project Cybersyn to Web 2.0 to DAO governance, regardless of political context or intention. Drawing on cybernetics, cognitive science, and political theory, the paper traces this assumption historically and examines its consequences. Platforms became more effective than democratic digital projects not by betraying the utopian promise but by abandoning the rationalist subject model. Standard responses to the crisis-regulation, digital literacy, democratic design-tend to reproduce the same baseline assumption they are meant to overcome.

title: Tracking Shifts in U.S. Monetary Policy: Comparing Multiplicative Indicator Saturation with Three Alternatives
affiliations: Babson College - Economics Division

detail.title: Tracking Shifts in U.S. Monetary Policy: Comparing Multiplicative Indicator Saturation with Three Alternatives
detail.abstract: This paper applies Multiplicative Indicator Saturation (MIS), for automated coefficient break selection, to a Taylor rule estimated with real-time data and the shadow federal funds rate from 1972 to 2025. MIS is compared with three approaches: sample splitting by Fed Chair, Bai-Perron break tests, and Markov-switching. MIS offers advantages by controlling for outliers and allowing parameters to vary flexibly over time. Across statistical methods and specifications, several breaks emerge as robust, most notably Volcker's and Greenspan's appointments. Surprisingly, once interest rate smoothing is incorporated, none of the statistical tests can reject a constant policy "rule" after 2000, even though this period is often described as a "new discretionary era."

title: A Multi-Input Approach to Markup Estimation: Evidence on Stability and Invariance
affiliations: Yanbian University

detail.title: A Multi-Input Approach to Markup Estimation: Evidence on Stability and Invariance
detail.abstract: This paper derives a multi-input integrated markup equation to address the input-selection problem inherent in conventional single-input markup estimation. The proposed framework incorporates capital, labor, domestic intermediates, and foreign intermediates, constructing markups from the full production cost structure. Using Korean manufacturing data from 1975-2023, we compare markup estimates across alternative classifications of intermediate inputs. The results show that the multi-input markup measure is highly stable and exhibits fragmentation invariance, whereas single-input measures are considerably more volatile and sensitive to specification. These findings highlight the importance of explicitly accounting for input heterogeneity in markup measurement, particularly in import-dependent small open economies.

detail.title: Greenwashing Risks for the Luxembourg Real Estate Sector

publicationDetails.detailsText: Revue luxembourgeoise de droit immobilier, No. 18

detail.abstract: Climate change is disrupting living conditions and economic activities with increasing frequency. This has led the public opinion to raise awareness of the issue and put pressure on governments and companies to take seriously risks stemming from the worsening of climate conditions due to the overexploitation of natural resources and excessive pollution of the planet. In this context, the real estate sector is perceived globally as the most polluting sector and the one characterised by the highest level of complexity for the achievement of an effective decarbonisation within EU and global targets. As a result, it can be inferred that this sector is largely exposed to greenwashing in the way that consumers’ preferences do not match the offers or declarations of operators regarding the environmental sustainability of their products and services. This study aims to identify greenwashing risks in the real estate sector by taking Luxembourg as a reference country within a broader European perspective as the EU has shown a proactive stance towards the challenge of the transition to the ‘Net Zero’ both from the financing and regulatory point of view. In fact, the legal analysis undertaken in this article will reveal that legislation at the EU level acts as a bond and an inspirer for national strategies and objectives aimed at countering the phenomenon of greenwashing.

detail.abstract: Wall Street's dominant algorithmic finance platforms-JPMorgan's derivative pricing engine, Goldman Sachs's Monte Carlo risk tools, BlackRock's Aladdin, and D-Wave/IBM quantum optimisers-share a fundamental structural limitation: they operate at the micro-level of individual financial instruments, single portfolios, or isolated institutions within a purely nominal framework. A systematic review of their published capabilities reveals five critical gaps: none addresses derivative exposure at the systemic sovereign level; none detects rehypothecation chain risk; none models algorithmic herding as an endogenous systemic force; none optimises sovereign wealth fund portfolios in real-asset space; and none predicts financial crises more than days ahead. This paper demonstrates that SVWORLD Standard 73.5 v1.9 (CVR73) addresses all five gaps through a structural real-asset architecture. Specifically: (i) the Netting and Rehypothecation Factor (NREF) detected systemic derivative risk 13 months before the 2008 Global Financial Crisis while JPMorgan's pricing tools showed no signal; (ii) the BANKING-73.5 Asset Quality Index (AQI) provides a four-dimensional real-asset portfolio optimisation surface that identified Silicon Valley Bank's insolvency 9 months before failure while Basel III metrics showed green; (iii) the seven-block B1-B7 structure constitutes the first portfolio optimisation framework native to sovereign wealth fund asset classes; (iv) the AI Correlation Multiplier (ACM) models algorithmic herding as an endogenous penalty validated in the 2022 UK LDI crisis; and (v) the CRYPTO-73.5 module anchors digital asset valuation to physical security constraints absent from any existing platform. We further present a five-stage computational roadmap (2026-2031) for CVR73 advanced implementation-from collateral netting optimisation to sovereign wealth portfolio allocation-demonstrating that CVR73's real-asset architecture was pre-adapted for the next generation of advanced computational finance.

detail.abstract: In this paper, we examine the impact of a price limit policy on skewness and the mispricing of high skewness stocks, leveraging a regulatory reform that relaxed daily price limits for stocks on China's the Growth Enterprises Board (hereafter ChiNext Board) from 10% to 20%. Following the reform, the skewness of ChiNext board stocks increased because of the short-sale constraint. Moreover, the skewness anomaly intensified on the ChiNext board but weakened on the Main Board, primarily driven by the rise in overpricing among high skewness stocks. The shift can be largely attributed to retail investors, whose optimism after upper limit hitting events is heighted by the reform. Moreover, by utilizing lottery data and IPO subscription data in China, we find that the relaxation of price limits enhances the attractiveness of ChiNext stocks as substitutes for lottery-seeking investments.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI), hyperscale cloud computing, and high-performance digital workloads has fundamentally transformed electricity demand patterns in the United States. Data centers are no longer marginal industrial consumers; they are emerging as giga-scale, continuous-load energy infrastructures that significantly influence regional grid planning, wholesale pricing dynamics, and transmission investment cycles.This paper develops a resource-driven optimization framework for integrating solar photovoltaic (PV) generation and battery energy storage systems (BESS) into high-demand digital infrastructure. detail.abstract: Article 173-VI of France’s Energy Transition for Green Growth Act requires large mutual funds to be transparent about the impacts of their investments on climate change. This article investigates whether this regulation helps discipline fund managers to reduce their carbon footprints. Using a difference-in-difference method, we show that French funds reduced their carbon footprints more after the introduction of the law. They rebalance their portfolios toward more climate-conscious firms. Mutual funds were incited to follow the regulation for reputation concerns.

detail.title: Green Finance,CBAM and Low-Carbon Economy: A DSGE Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper embeds green finance and the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) into a DSGE model featuring heterogeneous high‑/low‑carbon sectors, a green financial sector, and China‑EU bilateral openness. The model accounts for differentiated financing premiums, CBAM shocks, and China’s institutional features including local government growth preferences and nonlinear financing constraints. Based on 2000‑2024 Chinese macro data, we employ parameter calibration and Bayesian estimation to examine policy effects via impulse responses and scenario simulations. Results show that CBAM alone reduces emissions but causes short‑run contraction; green finance alone stabilizes growth but delivers limited abatement. Their coordination significantly improves low‑carbon output and emission efficiency, achieving carbon reduction and steady growth simultaneously. The synergy operates through dual cost pressures, cross‑sector factor reallocation, export structure upgrading, and factor misallocation correction. Heterogeneous effects are stronger in carbon‑intensive, low‑green‑technology, and high‑openness industries, as well as regions with pro‑green governments and developed financial markets. Green finance also hedges CBAM’s cross‑border contractionary shocks. This study provides quantitative implications for China to address CBAM and fulfill its Dual Carbon goals.

title: From End-of-Pipe to Supply Chain Greening: The Impact of Air Pollution Control Regulation on Corporate Green Supply Chain Construction

detail.title: From End-of-Pipe to Supply Chain Greening: The Impact of Air Pollution Control Regulation on Corporate Green Supply Chain Construction
detail.abstract: Whether environmental regulation can induce firms to move from end-of-pipe pollution control to green coordination across the entire supply chain is a crucial question for understanding corporate green transformation. Taking the "Air Ten Measures" (the Air Pollution Prevention and Control Action Plan) and subsequent local regulatory policies as a quasi-natural experiment, this paper uses data on China's A-share listed companies from 2008 to 2024 and employs a staggered difference-in-differences model to examine the impact of regulatory policies on firms' green supply chain construction level. The study finds that regulatory policies significantly improve firms' green supply chain construction level. In terms of mechanism, on the one hand, regulatory policies reshape firms' internal green governance capacity by strengthening management's green awareness, enhancing green innovation capability, and optimizing supply chain management efficiency; on the other hand, they improve firms' external green resource allocation by attracting green investors, thereby jointly promoting the upgrading of green supply chains. Further analysis reveals that the policy effects are robust across industries and regions with varying levels of pollution intensity. This paper extends the research on the microeconomic consequences of environmental regulation and green supply chain governance, and also provides empirical evidence for improving coordinated policies on green manufacturing, green distribution, and green consumption.

detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of firm-level perception of climate policy uncertainty (FCPU) on corporate total factor productivity (TFP). By constructing a granular index using word embedding to specifically capture the ambiguity and adverse shock dimensions of uncertainty, we isolate the downside risks of policy unpredictability. Our results show a significant negative effect of FCPU on TFP. The robustness of this finding is confirmed against potential endogeneity concerns using an instrumental variable, as well as through various alternative specifications, including different measures of uncertainty, additional fixed effects, altered sample periods, and lagged regressors. Our heterogeneity analysis reveals that this negative effect is more pronounced for state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and for firms located in regions with poorer air quality. We further trace the productivity decline to deteriorating internal governance, diminished corporate disclosure, inhibited adoption of green technologies, and widening maturity gaps between capital investments and financing sources. This study contributes to the literature by providing a risk-centric perspective on micro-level climate uncertainty. We demonstrate that the fear of ambiguity, distinct from general policy awareness, acts as a significant impediment to corporate sustainable growth.

title: Topological Early-Warning Signals for SystemicFinancial Crises:An Adaptive Real-Time Surveillance System

detail.title: Topological Early-Warning Signals for SystemicFinancial Crises:An Adaptive Real-Time Surveillance System
detail.abstract: Financial crises remain a persistent threat to economic stability, and conventional early-warningtools often fail to provide timely, reliable alerts. We present an adaptive real-time surveillance system that transforms the topological indicators of the Bubble–Crash Phase Transition Theorem—the topological susceptibility χtop and the market spectral gap λ1—into anoperational monitoring framework for systemic risk. The pipeline ingests ten macro-financialseries, reconstructs the market attractor via multi-asset time-delay embedding, and computes both indicators over rolling windows. An adaptive alert logic, based on a rollingmedian baseline, flags anomalous deformations of the attractor without requiring crisis-datelabels. In a historical backtest spanning 2017–2023, the system detects two out of threemajor crises (COVID-2020 and the 2022 bond rout) with zero false positives, a hit rateof 67%, and an average lead time of 10.8 months. Statistical significance is confirmed byphase-randomised surrogate tests (p < 0.001). A real-time application on 13 May 2026issued an alert driven by an extreme oil price spike and falling economic policy uncertainty,illustrating a deformation without rupture. The system outperforms widely used composite stress indicators in terms of both false-positive rate and lead time, and can serve as acomplementary financial-stability pillar alongside traditional Taylor-type monetary rules.

title: Investment in Power Generation Projects Under Multi-Market Uncertainty and Policy Impacts

detail.title: Investment in Power Generation Projects Under Multi-Market Uncertainty and Policy Impacts
detail.abstract: This paper constructs a real options model incorporating three stochastic factors: electricity price, carbon price, and green certificate price, to investigate how investors make optimal investment decisions between renewable and thermal power technologies under the influence of multi-market uncertainty and policies. The model simultaneously accounts for the impacts of policy instruments such as subsidies, carbon taxes, and carbon allowances on the investment boundaries. The study shows that carbon taxes and carbon allowances significantly affect the relative competitiveness of the two technologies by altering the marginal costs and revenue composition of thermal power. Although price subsidies and investment subsidies can lower the investment threshold for renewable energy, their marginal utility decreases as the subsidy level increases. Furthermore, the technology substitution effect is particularly pronounced in non-portfolio investment scenarios, where thermal power, as a substitute technology, can crowd out renewable energy investment. In contrast, the portfolio investment strategy, which incorporates capacity compensation, can effectively diversify the price fluctuation risks across multiple markets, significantly compressing the waiting region and enhancing the robustness of investment decisions. This paper provides a new quantitative basis for understanding green energy investment decisions under the coupling of electricity-carbon-green certificate markets.

title: The Dynamic Common Correlated Effects Estimation of Budget Neutral Environmental Policy & Risk Preference-With Application to Africa and Policy Contrast with the OECD.

detail.title: The Dynamic Common Correlated Effects Estimation of Budget Neutral Environmental Policy & Risk Preference-With Application to Africa and Policy Contrast with the OECD.
detail.abstract: We examine the effects of self-financing environmental taxation-subsidy policies on growth for advanced and emerging countries. First, we present a model-guided approach to structural change in growth transitions, with neutral climate-risk preferences between high- and low-carbon-intensive goods. We then explore CO2-reducing policy using a dynamic common correlated effects (DCCE) estimator based on a demeaned tax-subsidy formulation that identifies periods of increasing CO2 emissions by negative log-differences and periods of decreasing CO2 emissions by positive logdifferences in the policy-modified CO2 series. Applied to a sample of 24 African economies over 1990- 2022, the DCCE long-run homogeneity assumption cannot be rejected, revealing statistically significant positive emission-reducing policy impacts on output. We also find that the DCCE estimator for Africa performs better than the pooled mean group (PMG) estimator [0.441 (130.65) v. 0.153 (3.37)], respectively. Next, we compare the preferred DCCE specifications for Africa and the OECD, the latter based on a sample of 28 countries, 1990-2022. The outcome suggests larger policy DCCE slope estimates, [0.488 (67.12) v. 0.441 (130.65)]; larger error correction coefficients [-0.067 (5.45) v. -0.026 (3.22)], respectively, of Africa v. the OECD. The tests of equality for differences in cross-coefficients are rejected, indicating the emission diminishing budget neutral policy adoption benefits emerging economies in this study more than advanced economies; a discussion section points a) to a parallel bigger DCCE coefficient with similar test results for human capital on growth in Africa v. the OECD; b) we also discuss a possible explanation in difference for policy impact by a lock-in hypotheses of high and low brown fuel economies. Our results are consistent with the model-guided approach’s predictions and simulation outcomes.

detail.abstract: Small businesses in emerging economies often face difficulty accessing formal credit because lenders cannot easily evaluate borrower quality. This challenge is particularly relevant for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) operating within organised franchise and licensing networks. Unlike standalone MSMEs, franchise-affiliated businesses function within systems characterised by royalty payments, operational audits, compliance processes, and digitally maintained transaction records. These activities generate recurring operational information that may reflect business discipline, continuity, and governance quality. However, lenders often continue to assess such businesses using frameworks designed mainly for informationally opaque independent enterprises. This paper describes this problem as the governance-scoring disconnect. To address this gap, the paper introduces the Contractual Affiliation and Fee-based Liquidity Ecosystem (CAFLE) framework. Drawing on signalling theory and transaction cost economics, the framework explains how governance participation within franchise systems may improve borrower visibility through royalty continuity, governance-based transparency, and recurring compliance behaviour. Because many of these records are generated and monitored through ongoing governance systems, they may provide lenders with information that is less dependent on borrower self-reporting. The paper contributes to MSME finance and entrepreneurship research by examining franchise governance as a potential source of operational visibility within digitally evolving lending environments in emerging economies.

detail.abstract:
Crohn's disease perianal fistula (CD-AF) is among the most clinically intractable phenotypes of inflammatory bowel disease, with cumulative incidence of approximately 21% at 10 years and 26% at 20 years in Western population-based cohorts and substantially higher rates in East Asian populations. Despite anti-TNF biologics and expanded allogeneic mesenchymal stromal cell products such as darvadstrocel (Alofisel), durable fistula closure remains elusive in over half of treated patients. Umbilical-cord mesenchymal-stromal-cell (UC-MSC) exosomes represent an emerging cell-free regenerative platform with immunomodulatory, anti-fibrotic, and pro-angiogenic activity, simplified cold-chain logistics, and lower theoretical immunogenicity risk than parent cells.

A six-state Markov cohort model (quarterly cycles, 10-year horizon, 3% discount, half-cycle correction) was constructed in Microsoft Excel and independently re-implemented in Python. Comparators were infliximab, adalimumab, and surgical seton/LIFT. Efficacy inputs were derived from ACCENT-II, CHARM, a surgical network meta-analysis, and a pooled four-trial MSC-exosome dataset. Health-state utilities were drawn from Buxton et al. (2019). PSA used 2,000 Monte Carlo iterations.

UC-MSC exosome therapy was strictly dominant — lower discounted cost and higher discounted QALYs — across all nine head-to-head comparisons. Net monetary benefit at country-specific willingness-to-pay thresholds (US $150,000, CN $13,303, HK $54,107 per QALY) ranged from $9,082 (vs surgery in China) to $671,352 (vs infliximab in the United States). Five-year cumulative national net savings ranged from US $1.69 billion to $8.45 billion across pricing scenarios, with directionally consistent savings in Mainland China and Hong Kong SAR. PSA placed 99.7–100% of iterations in the cost-saving northwest quadrant for biologic comparisons and 87.7–96.2% for surgery comparisons. One-way deterministic sensitivity analyses confirmed dominance was robust to ±20% perturbation of every input parameter.

detail.abstract: For decades, behavioural economics has relied on experimental data alongside inductive and axiomatic reasoning to model choice under risk and resolve behavioural anomalies. While descriptively powerful, the probability weighting function used in prospect theory lacks a deductive mathematical microfoundation. Building on the recent framework of complex-valued economics, here we derive the inverse-S function by projecting linear probability p+q=1 onto the cognitive unit circle p2 + q2 = 1 in the complex plane. This geometric projection naturally reproduces empirical probability distortion and yields subcertainty as a Pythagorean penalty. Grounded in the principle of the marginal rate of substitution (MRS), this finding suggests that behavioural anomalies—long studied as systematic deviations from rationality—may instead emerge from the natural mathematics of optimisation operating in the complex plane.  By extending our  minimal-assumption PDE framework of utility maximisation (β2∂x2U = ∂y2U), this unified decision theory formalises behavioural economics and integrates it with classical economic theory.

detail.abstract: Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) constitute the leading and most rapidly accelerating cause of preventable mortality across sub-Saharan Africa, yet the clinical artificial intelligence literature has overwhelmingly neglected both the African epidemiological context and the algorithmic fairness implications of deploying machine learning models in demographically distinct, resource-constrained clinical environments. This paper presents the first systematic review and empirical analysis of algorithmic fairness in clinical machine learning for NCD prediction specifically oriented toward sub-Saharan Africa. Following a PRISMA-inspired protocol, 47 studies published between 2015 and 2026 were identified, screened, and analyzed. Key finding: only 8 of 47 studies (17.0%) included any form of fairness evaluation, only 3 (6.4%) employed formal fairness metrics, and only 12 (25.5%) were conducted on African patient data. The systematic review is enriched by original empirical evidence drawn from the author's prior peer-reviewed studies on Type 2 diabetes prediction (AUC-ROC = 0.8226, significant BMI subgroup recall disparities) and cardiovascular disease prediction (AUC-ROC = 0.9270, 5.92 percentage point female recall deficit), forming the first multi-disease empirical fairness dataset for NCD prediction in West Africa. Based on this synthesis, a five-pillar research agenda is proposed addressing the data representation crisis, the fairness measurement gap, the explainability requirement, the deployment infrastructure barrier, and the sex and demographic bias emergency in clinical AI. This work constitutes the scientific and ethical foundation for a new paradigm of equity-centered clinical AI research and development for sub-Saharan Africa.

detail.abstract:
Background: Empathy in healthcare has been shown to benefit patients and practitioners, but can be inhibited by system-level barriers. No measure of system-level empathy in healthcare has been developed. We therefore aimed to develop an index that quantifies system-level empathy and test whether higher levels of empathy within National Health Service (NHS) trusts are associated with better patient, staff, and financial outcomes.

Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study of NHS trusts. Drawing on an established model of system-level empathy, we developed a healthcare “system empathy index”, including nine domains: fostering a culture of empathy, leadership with compassion, teamwork, appropriate physical environment, sensible workload, adequate time, effective leadership, practitioner empathy, and wellbeing. We obtained item scores using publicly available sources, including the NHS Staff Survey, Care Quality Commission (CQC), and Trust Accounts Consolidation (TAC) data. An overall rating from 1 to 10 was then generated for the trusts. We explored associations between index scores and patient outcomes (CQC safety and effectiveness ratings), practitioner outcomes (sickness and absence and self-reported health), and trust financial outcomes (from NHS TAC data). We used meta-regression for proportion outcomes with inverse variance weighting.

Results: The average overall system empathy score was 5.99 (range: 4.88 to 6.78). Higher scores were associated with improved patient outcomes. A 0.25-unit (2.5%) increase in index score was associated with 76% higher odds of trusts being rated good or outstanding for safety (p<0.001) and 46% greater odds of trusts being rated good or outstanding for effectiveness (p=0.003). A 0.25-unit increase in index score was also associated with improved staff outcomes, including reduced sickness and absenteeism (β=0.20, p=0.004), better self-reported health (β=0.21, p<0.001), and lower burnout (β=0.21, p<0.001). Higher empathy scores were associated with lower expenditure on temporary staffing (p=0.012) and consultancy (p=0.024).

Conclusions: We developed a novel system empathy index and found that higher empathy is associated with better patient, staff, and some financial outcomes. These findings support the importance of system-level factors in healthcare performance. Empathy training at a system level is likely to improve outcomes, although further research is needed to establish causality and validate the index in independent datasets.

detail.abstract: What implications might rising animosity towards political out-partisans have for public health? Vaccination has a significant social aspect, protecting not only the vaccinated, but also those around them. While political ideology in the United States was an important driver of individuals’ willingness to get vaccinated against COVID-19, with those on the political right displaying greater hesitancy, we examine the role that political diversity has on vaccine uptake across US states and commuting zones. Using data from the Cooperative Election Study fielded on over 20,000 respondents in November 2021, and controlling for individual partisanship, we find that those who are political outliers in their community are significantly less likely to get vaccinated. By contrast, we find no equivalent negative effect for ethnic diversity. In sum, the impact of affective polarization is not limited to encounters between non-partisans; it can lead to decreased pro-social behavior that harms political friends and foes alike. Yet these behavioral effects depend on how individuals relate to their community’s predominant political ideology.

Objective: Conservatively quantify the public health and economic damages of low-quality generic drugs on chronic disease management in the United States based on available studies, and review health system solutions to avoid low-quality and incentivize high-quality generics.  

Data Sources: Generic drug quality is an evolving but sparse field of research; therefore, the expertise of 21 experts with experience in the field were relied upon to identify meaningful areas of existing research within chronic disease, where medication issues are expected to be most pronounced due to longevity and persistence of treatment. Four diseases (epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, atherosclerosis, and hypertension) were chosen by the group due to the relative abundance of informative studies and the diversity of the diseases. A chronological review of published health system solutions was also performed. 

Data Synthesis / Results: Extrapolating from studies in these four chronic diseases and focusing on the most directly observable 10% low-quality generic drugs, we conservatively estimate the 2024 economic burden of this low-quality subset of generic drugs at $18.4 billion growing to $238 billion over the next 10 years if not addressed, largely due to many thousands of avoidable serious adverse events like disease relapse and hospitalizations. Potential solutions are discussed that may enable a market correction to avoid the low-quality generic drugs and incentivize continuous product improvement. 

Conclusion and Relevance: This novel review represents the first broad population analysis of the substantial economic and public health impact from low-quality generic drugs and synthesizes modern approaches to addressing this largely underappreciated issue. Real-world approaches are reviewed where pharmacy practice can be modified to help ensure only the highest-quality generics are dispensed to patients to improve outcomes and reduce waste.

title: Hollowing Out The Head:A Theoretical Analysis of AI-Driven Asymmetric Flattening in Labour Market Polarization

detail.title: Hollowing Out The Head:A Theoretical Analysis of AI-Driven Asymmetric Flattening in Labour Market Polarization
detail.abstract: This paper develops a general equilibrium theoretical framework to analyze how artificial intelligence (AI) adoption restructures traditional labour market polarization. While Routine-Biased Technical Change (RBTC) historically produced a U-shaped employment distribution by automating middle-skill routine tasks, contemporary generative AI targets non-routine cognitive functions, fundamentally altering the skill premium and task composition of work. Integrating the Acemoglu-Restrepo task-based model with Autor's expertise automation framework, I formalize three core mechanisms: cognitive task displacement, productivity-driven demand reallocation, and the reinstatement of novel high-complexity roles. The model demonstrates that AI induces an asymmetric flattening of the wage distribution, characterized by wage compression and skill depreciation at the upper-middle tier, continued erosion of administrative roles, and relative insulation of low-skill manual occupations driven by the asymmetric elasticity of substitution between cognitive and physical labour. Furthermore, I show that directed technical change shifts intra-firm rents from marginal labour to capital owners and AI system designers, exacerbating functional income inequality and altering wage-setting dynamics in cognitive-intensive sectors. The analysis concludes with a theoretical welfare evaluation of labour market policies, arguing for targeted wage insurance, modular lifelong learning accounts, and marginal tax recalibration to mitigate transition frictions without distorting productivity incentives. This project contributes to modern labour economics by formalizing the transition from routine-biased to expertise-biased technological change, providing a rigorous foundation for future empirical calibration and policy design in AI-integrated economies.

Employment, Economic Value, and Community Integration

Data Factories and Modern Data Centres: 
Employment, Economic Value, and Community Integration
detail.abstract:
Data Factories (high-performance data centres designed to support advanced computing workloads) are becoming foundational infrastructure for economic productivity, scientific research, public services, and national resilience. As demand worldwide for this infrastructure grows, proposed projects increasingly encounter community-level concerns related to employment, environmental impact, electricity pricing, water use, and local disruption.

This paper provides an evidence-based assessment of the employment, economic, and infrastructure implications of Data Factories across their full lifecycle, drawing on data from European member states, international energy agencies, utility regulators, and academic research. Beyond project-level impacts, it examines the local, regional, and national consequences of participation or non-participation in advanced computing infrastructure deployment.

The analysis finds that, when responsibly planned and operated, Modern Data Centres function as long-lived enabling infrastructure, supporting workforce retention, fiscal stability, and infrastructure modernisation at the community and regional level, while strengthening national competitiveness and capacity. Conversely, sustained resistance or delay does not eliminate demand for AI infrastructure but instead redirects investment, employment, and strategic capability to other jurisdictions, increasing long-term opportunity costs and infrastructure divergence.

detail.abstract: Emotional distress among adult cancer patients is widely recognized, yet its identification does not consistently lead to coordinated psychosocial care. Despite recommendations for routine distress screening, gaps persist due to fragmented workflows, competing clinical priorities, and limited integration of psychosocial services within oncology settings. This manuscript proposes advocacy mapping as a trauma-informed, structurally grounded framework to support more coordinated responses to psychosocial needs. Drawing on structural and anti-oppressive perspectives, advocacy mapping is conceptualized as a method for organizing goals, stakeholder roles, and care pathways across levels of practice. The framework highlights the role of oncology social workers in translating patient-identified needs into structured advocacy priorities and facilitating alignment across interdisciplinary teams and systems of care. Implications for practice suggest that advocacy mapping may strengthen coordination between distress identification, referral processes, and psychosocial interventions, while supporting greater integration of care within oncology systems. As a conceptual manuscript, this paper does not include empirical evaluation but outlines considerations for future implementation and assessment. Overall, advocacy mapping offers a structured approach to addressing gaps between the identification of psychosocial needs and the delivery of coordinated, system-level responses in oncology care.

detail.abstract: Standard economic theory, built exclusively on instrumental rationality (means-end calculation for material efficiency), cannot explain the explosive growth of the digital social economy nor resolve the persistent Solow paradox: massivecomputing & AI investments have failed to deliver corresponding productivity gains; to address this, we develop a new ontological foundation for economics based on phenomenal consciousness (qualia)—ultimate source of value—grounded in mathematical logic & thermodynamics, proving no formalized system (including Turing machines & AI) can self-maintain (as it entails the unsolvable halting problem), introducing a hierarchical non-formalized capital structure (consciousness, tacit knowledge, consensus) residing in human minds and irreplicable by formalized systems, and showing consciousness is the only known source of negentropy (order) in economies, physical foundation of value. We construct a dual-rationality general equilibrium model integrating instrumental and communicative rationality (with a feedback loop: individual experience generates tacit knowledge, which aggregates into consensus, which shapes technological progress, transforming experience) and prove four core theorems: (1) Non-Substitutability—AI cannot substitute for humans as value creation subjects; (2) Structural Transformation—As AI automates the formalized instrumental sector, the non-formalized communicative sector dominates value and employment; (3) Solow Paradox—When formalized capital outgrows non-formalized capital, its marginal product declines without standard diminishing returns; (4) Consensus Capital Externality—Markets systematically underinvest in non-formalized capital; this framework explains Solow paradox—exponential formalized capital growth outpaces slow non-formalized growth, leading to sharply diminishing returns and formalization idling—and shows long-run growth is constrained not by technology or resources, but by limited human consciousness capital; the AI revolution does not eliminate labor—it makes human subjectivity more valuable than ever.

Game theory begins as a branch of mathematics. A theorem proves the existence of a xed point and is titled system of equations. Its English translation becomes general economic equilibrium. The added word equilibrium is a label, not physics. Economists inherit the formalism and, at each step, relabel the topological conditions of the theorem as properties of the real economy but these properties, posited agent by agent, do not survive the passage to the market, as will be demonstrated twenty years later. 
      This essay traces the fracture. A logical tradition in Central Europe had laid the foundations in the nineteenth century: the distinction between form and meaning, between syntax and physics. The twentieth century the century of wars destroyed it, word by word, label by label, until the global economy was steered by weightless xed points.
      At the start of the twenty-rst century, an anonymous author attempts the rst repair: a protocol based on Proof of Work that anchors an irreversible energy cost to any attempt at rewriting. The link is physical.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the economic rationale and multi-dimensional consequences of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's May 2026 appeal to Indian citizens to abstain from purchasing gold for one year, accompanied by the government's simultaneous decision to double gold import duties from 6% to 15%. Drawing on 100 years of Indian monetary history-from the Gold Control Act of 1962 through the 2013 duty cycle-this analysis evaluates the short-term and long-term impact on gold prices, the retail jewellery sector, employment, GDP, per capita income, and broader macroeconomic indicators. detail.abstract: This study investigates the role of the expert assessment – conducted by two analysts following the production of a rating based solely on the statistical model – within Banca d’Italia’s in-house credit assessment system of Italian non-financial firms (ICAS). We have two aims: to document recent methodological enhancements, including the integration of climate-related risks and of sector analysis, and to provide an estimate of the contribution of the expert assessment to the rating process. The study leverages over 25,000 assessments produced by analysts between 2016 and 2022, including corporate default events. The recent methodological innovations have enhanced the transparency and consistency of the expert assessment, facilitating the integration of new risk sources. Our empirical results show that the expert assessment significantly improves both the predictive power and the discriminatory power of the full ratings obtained through ICAS, compared with the ratings based solely on the statistical model, with an increase of the AUROC of around 2 percentage points. title: Taxation and Economic Growth: A Comparative Analysis of Asian and OECD Economies

detail.title: Taxation and Economic Growth: A Comparative Analysis of Asian and OECD Economies
detail.abstract:
This study analyses the impact of taxation on economic growth in ten Asian developing and ten OECD countries from 1991 to 2020 using Fixed Effects panel estimation. It tests whether fiscal policy models from advanced economies apply across different development contexts.

 The findings reveal key divergences. Corporate income taxes promote growth in OECD countries but have no effect in Asian economies. Trade taxes are positively associated with growth in both regions, challenging trade liberalization orthodoxy. Higher tax-to-GDP ratios boost growth in Asian countries but constrain it in OECD nations.

 These results challenge universal tax policy prescriptions and highlight the importance of institutional context. These results underscore the need for development-specific fiscal strategies that account for institutional capacity and structural differences between economies.

detail.abstract: We assess the cross-sectional relation between media coverage and cryptocurrency returns using 7.6 million news articles from a large-scale web corpus. We find that cryptocurrencies with no coverage earn higher risk-adjusted returns than those with high coverage. By decomposing coverage intensity into coverage breadth and novelty, we separate the dissemination of existing information from the arrival of new information. We show that media coverage combines two offsetting channels: breadth captures an attention-driven channel that predicts lower future returns, while novelty captures an information channel that predicts higher future returns. Our findings highlight the role of information diffusion in cryptocurrency returns.

detail.abstract:
The Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act of 2022 (EFAA) prohibits enforcement of pre-dispute arbitration agreements in cases involving sexual harassment or sexual assault. Spurred by the #MeToo movement, and enacted with broad bipartisan support, EFAA was intended to ensure that victims of harassment or assault may choose to pursue relief in court, rather than being forced in private arbitral proceedings.
 
This Article provides a detailed assessment of the first four years of litigation under the statute. It focuses on three inter-related interpretive questions that have arisen frequently. First, most courts are properly concluding that EFAA includes actions based on non-sexualized harassment, such as insults or sabotaging of work because of sex, as well as unwelcome sexualized conduct; it also includes harassment based on pregnancy or related medical conditions and based on sexual orientation or gender identity. Second, courts are properly holding that if any claim is within the ambit of EFAA, the entire case can be litigated in court. And third, while there is a lack of consensus as to whether the sufficiency of allegations in the complaint should be judged under a plausibility standard or a non-frivolous standard, courts are clear that under either standard what matters is the facts alleged, not the label affixed to the claims. 

The Article concludes that EFAA is living up to its billing. The law gives victims of harassment or assault the opportunity to seek relief in court, and it offers a workable model for broader reform limiting the use of forced arbitration more generally.

detail.abstract: Public sector Ombuds offices are an important part of the administrative justice system across common law jurisdictions today. They provide accessible and oft en effective recourse to persons who are aggrieved at public administrative decisions, and also broader systemic oversight of the conduct of public administration. But what happens when things go wrong  We can think of many examples. The Australian Ombudsman missed serious illegality in the infamous Robodebt scheme. A complainant may be aggrieved at their complaint being rejected at the initial triaging stage. An official may consider that they were wrongly criticised in an Ombuds office report. Should judicial review be available to address such issues? In some jurisdictions, the Ombuds office's work is protected by a privative clause. Should courts give any effect to such clauses? My frame of reference for addressing these questions is administrative justice. The question is what approach will promote good administrative decisionmaking, accessible and effective recourse for aggrieved individuals and effective implementation of the social objectives of administrative regimes. I propose a proportionality enquiry based on case law in other similar contexts. Applying that enquiry, I argue that, in terms of administrative justice, the disadvantages of judicial review of Ombuds office determinations outweigh the benefits in many contexts. Judicial review should be restricted or excluded in those contexts.

detail.abstract: This paper argues that modern corporations, particularly Big Tech Platform Corporations (BTPCs), should be understood not as private contractual arrangements but as artificial legal entities created and empowered by States. Through incorporation, corporations receive State-like attributes including perpetual existence, legal personhood, capital lock-in, and entity shielding, enabling them to accumulate and organise capital across time and space. The paper introduces the concepts of “Recursive Capital” and “Capital-Constituting Corporations” to explain how BTPCs extend beyond market participation to shape the very conditions under which economic activity becomes capitalisable. Drawing historical parallels with the English East India Company and Gilded Age monopolies, the paper contends that BTPCs now exercise infrastructural and governance power comparable to semi-sovereign actors. Existing antitrust and contractual theories are therefore inadequate. The paper concludes that platform governance requires structural regulation and a reassertion of democratic oversight to recalibrate the delegated powers States have granted corporations.

detail.abstract: Communication can facilitate coordination within teams in many competitive settings, from team sports to military operations. However, it may leak and reveal intentions to the opponent. We study how this tension shapes behaviour in a team contest, both theoretically and experimentally. Our theory predicts that secure communication plays a dual role: it improves internal coordination while concealing intentions from the opponent, thereby raising competition intensity-operationalized as effort investment-for all parties. Our experiment provides causal evidence for these effects. When communication leaks, its concealment role disappears, and teammates trade off coordination against predictability. When coordination concerns dominate, teammates should always communicate, but sometimes they choose not to, leading to costly coordination failures. Nevertheless, investment levels remain close to those under secure communication, well above the levels observed without communication. These results suggest that blocking an opponent's communication may be more effective than spying on it.

detail.abstract:
The first phase of the artificial-intelligence infrastructure trade was framed as a training-capacity problem: acquire accelerators, secure high-bandwidth memory, build clusters, and amortize capital expenditure over future model demand. The second phase is different. As model usage shifts toward persistent inference, lower unit prices can release enough latent demand that scarcity does not disappear; it migrates into memory, power delivery, interconnection queues, cooling, deployment timing, and monetization lag.

This working paper introduces the Inference Residual, a protocol-stage framework for testing whether cheaper inference reduces AI scarcity or relocates it into physical delivery constraints. We define the Token-to-Watt Basis (TWB) as a standardized growth-rate residual between token-velocity proxy momentum and effective power-delivery proxy momentum. TWB is not a raw ratio of tokens to watts and should not be cited as a live factor before both proxy legs are admitted under stable source boundaries. To handle lumpy infrastructure supply, we define usable inference capacity with a smooth-minimum bottleneck operator rather than a simple additive average. The contribution is conceptual and methodological: it turns the question “where did AI scarcity move?” into a falsifiable measurement protocol for weekly research use.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether the effectiveness of Basel regulation in reducing bank risk depends on the institutional quality of the country in which it is implemented. Using an unbalanced panel of 117 banks across 40 countries from 2005 to 2024, I estimate fixed-effects models with standard errors clustered at the country level. Neither Basel adoption intensity alone nor institutional quality alone achieves conventional significance as a determinant of non-performing loan (NPL) ratios. However, their interaction is negative and marginally significant (one-tailed p = 0.058), consistent with the hypothesis that Basel reduces NPLs only in strong-governance environments. Banks in weak-institution countries (e.g., Nigeria, Bangladesh) experience higher NPLs following Basel adoption; in strong-institution countries (e.g., Singapore, the Netherlands), the effect reverses. These findings suggest that harmonized global regulation cannot substitute for domestic institutional capacity, with direct implications for Basel IV design and financial reform sequencing in emerging economies.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes an equilibrium reinterpretation of housing price responsiveness to local income. Rather than treating housing price-income elasticity as a fixed structural parameter, the paper argues that responsiveness may itself depend on the composition of demand operating at the margin of the housing market. In supply-constrained housing markets with heterogeneous buyers, equilibrium prices are determined by buyers located at the margin of the willingness-to-pay distribution. When marginal demand becomes increasingly dominated by buyers whose purchasing capacity depends weakly on local economic conditions, equilibrium housing prices may become progressively less responsive to local income. The paper develops a parsimonious equilibrium framework formalizing this mechanism and evaluates its empirical implications using a municipality-year panel covering the 66 municipalities of the Balearic Islands over the 2015-2023 period. The empirical analysis combines local income measures with transaction-composition indicators capturing exposure to non-local demand, including foreign-buyer shares and legal-entity purchases. The results indicate that housing price responsiveness to local income weakens systematically in municipalities with greater exposure to externally anchored purchasing capacity. The attenuation becomes more pronounced in highly exposed demand regimes, consistent with the nonlinear implications of the framework. The findings suggest that observed housing price-income elasticities may reflect not only structural housing-market characteristics, but also variation in the composition of marginal demand operating at the equilibrium price, with potential implications for housing affordability and policy design in supply-constrained markets.
